input.brief: AFİNA ZEYTİN is an olive and olive-oil producer from Ellek, Düziçi, Osmaniye. The official slogan is Kökü toprakta. Yeri sofrada. Corporate production trust is 65 percent and real retail commerce is 35 percent. Preserve original logo, Fraunces/Figtree and olive-paper-champagne tokens. Existing assets: approved grove-to-branch Flow film and poster, approved representative branded packshots and product scenes, one real factory photograph with blurred plate. The distinctive signature is the real approved product packshot emerging from the grove as the slogan moves from roots to table, without changing packaging geometry. Four existing product families and six variants, with detail/cart/account links; never invent prices, testimonials, certificates, capacity or production footage. Production facility and provenance are the evidence. No paid media, no new assets, native scroll, motion/react only, poster reduced-motion fallback and keyboard-accessible actions.

direction.name: The page is the object
direction.idea: Find the printed or physical artefact that already exists in the subject's world and build the page as that thing. A wedding site is the invitation card. A restaurant is its menu. A conference is the ticket; a record is its sleeve; a shop is the receipt or the swing tag; an archive is a stack of tabbed folders; a course is the syllabus sheet. The artefact supplies everything a template would otherwise invent: its proportions, its typographic manners, its way of grouping information. Visitors recognise the object instantly, which is why these pages feel specific.
direction.composition: The first screen shows the artefact as a single filled panel (paper colour on a contrasting ground) centred or offset, with believable proportions: a card at 5:7, a ticket at about 2.2:1 with a notch cut by `clip-path`, a menu as a tall sheet. All primary content lives on it, set the way that object is set: centred and symmetrical for an invitation, in tidy aligned columns for a menu or ticket. The ground behind is a flat colour or one full-bleed photograph. As the page continues, each section is another piece of the same stationery: a second card, a tear-off stub, a folded panel, always filled shapes with real edges (straight, notched, scalloped, perforated by a dotted `border` of round dots at 4px or more), never outlined boxes. The footer is the back of the object.
direction.typography: Take the manners of the artefact: a bookish serif with small caps avoided, or a blunt condensed face for tickets and posters. Sizes stay within what print would use relative to the panel; the name is large on the panel, details are small and exact.
direction.colour: Paper and ink plus the ground the paper sits on. Two or three flat colours in total, like a two-colour print job.
direction.imagery: Optional. One photograph behind the object, or small photographs placed on it like tipped-in plates. The object itself is the image.
direction.richness: Recognition. The shaped edges, the print-like alignment and the limited inks make a familiar object out of plain HTML.
direction.pitfalls: Choose an artefact that truly belongs to the subject, or it becomes costume. Shape the edges with fills and `clip-path`; an outlined rectangle with a thin border is not an object. Keep text sizes readable on a phone, where the object becomes full width with its shaped edge kept at top and bottom.

hero.name: Invitation card, cropped
hero.blueprint: A flat field of one soft colour fills the viewport. Centred on it is a single portrait card in paper colour, 5:7, on columns 4–9, its top edge 190px down and its lower third cut off by the bottom of the viewport, so the page visibly continues as the rest of the card. The card is a filled shape with scalloped inner corners, made with `clip-path` or with four corner circles in the field colour, and no outline. Inside, with 56px padding, everything is centred and symmetrical like letterpress stationery. The two names, or the title, are set in a large italic serif at clamp(56px, 5.6vw, 88px) on two lines, staggered so line one sits left of centre and line two right. Between and beneath them, date, time and place appear as short lines at 15px in sentence case, separated by space and by one solid 10px diamond. The top row sits on the field above the card at 28px margins: a small monogram top-left, three text links centred, and the single action, a solid rectangular button in the ink colour, top-right.
hero.mobile: The card becomes full width minus 12px margins, starts 96px down and is still cropped by the bottom edge, with its scalloped top corners kept. The names stay on two lines at 12vw, centred without the stagger, and the details follow at 15px. The monogram sits top-left and the action button top-right on the field; the three links move onto the card's lower part, below the fold.
hero.headline: The two names or the title on two lines, up to about 12 characters per line, set as they would be printed on the card.

photos.title: Objects
photos.note: single objects seen close: instruments, tools, cameras, books

photos.alt: Open book lying on a wooden table in soft light
Close-up of metal fork tines against a dark blurred background
Black vintage typewriter with blank paper seen from above on white
Steam rising from a metal mug with blurred blue background
Close-up of a turntable tonearm resting on a vinyl record
Cup of coffee seen from above on a bright red surface
Pine cones resting on weathered wood in black and white
Close-up of an analogue clock face in black and white

motion.name: Curtain footer
motion.description: The page content slides up like a sheet to uncover the footer waiting beneath it, so the last screen is revealed rather than scrolled to. Build with a sticky footer at the bottom and a main element with its own background and a higher stacking order. No JavaScript.

sections.name: Title, note, facts row
sections.blueprint: First row: a heading of two to four words in a light weight at clamp(44px, 5vw, 76px) sits on the left margin in columns 1–6; a three-line paragraph at 16px, 260px wide, sits in columns 10–12 with its last line on the heading's baseline. Columns 7–9 stay empty. 120px lower, a second row sets three or four facts (a date, a time, a place, a price) as large light text at clamp(28px, 3vw, 44px), spread across the 12 columns with `justify-content: space-between`. Each fact has a one-line explanation at 14px directly under it in the soft ink, left-aligned to the fact. Facts are separated only by the space between them, so the row reads like the line of times on a printed programme. A photograph may start under the right half of the facts row, 5 columns wide at 4:3. Padding 140px top, 120px bottom.
sections.mobile: Heading at 11vw on the left margin; the note follows directly under it at 16px, full width. The facts become a two-column grid with a 32px row gap, each fact at 26px with its explanation beneath. Any photograph goes last, full width.

sections.name: Heading captions a panorama (borrowed from intro)
sections.blueprint: The section is exactly 100svh. Its top third holds a two-line heading of three to six words at clamp(48px, 6.5vw, 96px) with leading 0.95, either centred or flush left on the page margin. 28px beneath the heading sit two small captions side by side, each two lines at 13px and 150px wide with a 48px gap, aligned to the heading (centred as a pair, or both starting at its left edge). 40px below them a full-bleed photograph begins and runs off the bottom of the viewport: it is 100vw wide at 21:9 or wider, and only its top 55–60svh is visible before the fold, the rest arriving with scroll. The heading therefore reads as a large caption to the picture. On an object-led page the image is the object on a flat dark panel inset by the page margin instead of bleeding to the edges.
sections.mobile: Heading at 12vw on two lines, left-aligned, taking the top 30% of the screen. The two captions merge into one four-line block at 14px. The photograph begins at 45% of the screen height in a 4:5 crop, full-bleed, and runs off the bottom.

sections.name: Specimens on colour tiles (borrowed from features)
sections.blueprint: Each capability is represented by one object photographed alone and shown on a flat colour tile. Columns 1–3 hold the heading (two to four words at 40–52px), top-aligned, with a 30ch sentence beneath and nothing else down the rest of that column. Columns 4–12 hold a grid of five or six tiles in two rows with 10px gaps: tiles are 4:5 except one, which is double width at 8:5 and placed second in the first row. Tile colours rotate through three palette fields. Each photograph is centred at about 70% of its tile's height; on light tiles use mix-blend-mode: multiply so a white studio background disappears. Under each tile, outside it and aligned to its left edge: the capability name at 20px medium and one fact at 16px in the soft ink. No text on the tiles and no hover lift.
sections.mobile: The heading and its sentence sit on top at full width. Tiles become a two-column grid with 8px gaps; the double tile spans both columns at 8:5 and comes first. Names shrink to 17px and facts to 15px, still under each tile.

sections.name: Drag row of moments
sections.blueprint: A story told left to right. Top row: the heading, two to four words at 28–36px, at the left margin; at the right margin two solid square buttons, 48px each, for back and forward. Directly beneath, a solid bar 6px tall spans the full width in a soft tone, with a full-ink segment showing how far the row has been scrolled. Then the row itself: six to nine columns, each 280px wide with 32px gaps, in a horizontally scrolling flex container with scroll-snap that bleeds off both viewport edges. Every column reads top to bottom: a one-line caption at 18px bold that carries the order in words ('We met', 'Two winters on', 'The move'), three lines at 15px in the soft ink, then 80–140px of empty space that varies per column, then a 4:5 portrait photograph. Because the spaces vary, the photographs' top edges rise and fall along the row.
sections.mobile: Columns are 72vw wide with 16px gaps, so the next one always shows at the right edge. The buttons are dropped; the 6px progress bar stays under the heading. The empty space inside columns shrinks to 32–64px but still varies from column to column.

sections.name: The reply card
sections.blueprint: The invitation to act is a printed card lying on the page. On a dark or strongly coloured flat field about 80svh tall, a paper-coloured panel 44vw wide with 7:5 proportions sits in columns 6–12, rotated two degrees, with its lower edge hanging 60px past the section's bottom so the section crops it. On the card, with 48px padding, everything is centred the way stationery is: a heading of two to four words at 32px, one or two lines at 17px, then the action as a solid bar across the card's full inner width, 56px tall, in the ink colour with paper-coloured text. Columns 1–4 hold only a short paragraph at 20–24px in the field's light ink, bottom-aligned 64px above the edge. The card is a plain filled rectangle with square corners and no outline; its rotation and crop make it an object.
sections.mobile: The paragraph comes first at 20px. The card follows at 90% width, tilted one degree, centred, its bottom edge still cropped by the section. Heading at 24px, lines at 16px, and the action bar 52px tall across the full inner width of the card.

sections.name: Tabbed index cards
sections.blueprint: Questions are filed like cards in a drawer. A heading of two to four words at about 4vw sits in columns 3–10. Beneath it, in the same columns, five or six filled panels are stacked so that each overlaps the one above, leaving 96px of every card showing. Each card has a tab on its top edge, 200px wide and 40px tall, stepping right by 150px per card, cut with `clip-path: polygon()` so card and tab are one filled shape. The cards rotate through two or three palette colours. The tab carries the topic in one or two words at 16px; the visible strip under it shows the question at 20px medium. Choosing a card expands it to show the answer at 17px over at most 50ch and pushes the cards below it down. One card is open at a time; the first is open on load.
sections.mobile: Cards run full width with the same overlap, 88px of each showing. Tabs shrink to 120px wide and step right by 48px per card. The open card expands in place with its answer at 16px and 20px padding, and the heading leads at 9vw.

sections.name: Visit card on a photograph
sections.blueprint: A full-bleed photograph of the place, 100vw by 100svh, carries one solid card and nothing else. The card is a filled panel in the paper colour, fully opaque, 380px wide with 8px corners and 32px padding, placed in the upper-right corner 60px from the top and right edges (or the upper-left: pick the corner where the photograph is calmest). It holds, top to bottom: a two- or three-word title at 28px in a light weight; the address on two lines at 16px; the opening hours as three rows with days at the left and times right-aligned in tabular figures; the phone number; then, flush with the card's bottom edge and spanning its width, a solid booking button 52px tall. The card may be `position: sticky; top: 60px` inside a taller section so it holds while the photograph scrolls beneath it. The photograph's focal point must stay clear of the card. No heading outside the card.
sections.mobile: The photograph is 100vw by 70svh. The card leaves the corner: it spans the width with 16px margins and overlaps the photograph's bottom edge by 80px, so image and card interlock. The booking button is full width, 56px tall, at the card's bottom.

sections.name: The back of the card
sections.blueprint: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
sections.mobile: The panel runs full width with six scallops across its top edge. The stamp sits top-right at 64px wide; the sign-off and message come first, then the address lines at 17px beneath them, then the imprint line centred at 12px.

references.name: ARCHIV
references.idea: A waitlist page as a museum plinth: one cut-out everyday object at a time, centred on off-white beneath a heavy serif wordmark.
references.hero: Off-white single screen with no scroll. A heavy high-contrast serif wordmark in black caps sits top-left at a 56px margin, about 410px wide (28% of the viewport) and 80px tall. Opposite, top-right at the same margin, one line of 14px sans description aligns with the wordmark's top. Dead centre, one photographed object (a painted wooden pepper mill about 140px wide and 440px tall) stands on a barely visible lighter rounded square with a soft contact shadow; other objects replace it in turn. Below, a centred 11px grey line, then a white rounded email field 236px wide with a circled arrow inside its right end. Roughly 80% is empty.
references.type: The wordmark is drawn lettering in a heavy display serif with tight spacing, cap height about 5.5vw. All live text is Helvetica Neue regular at 14px and about 11px, black or grey. Two text sizes only; the contrast is wordmark against near-invisible interface text.
references.colour: #f1efec #000000 #ffffff #d9261c #e8a317 #7a7a75 — Warm off-white field, black wordmark, a white input; all colour arrives through whichever object is showing (red and yellow mill, tan leather, blue cap).
references.imagery: Studio cut-outs of single everyday objects in three-quarter view with a soft grounded shadow on matching off-white, each scaled to similar visual mass and centred, one at a time, no frame.
references.layout: One fixed viewport with four elements: wordmark top-left, description top-right, object in the exact centre, form bottom-centre. Margins of 56px, no rules, nav or footer. On mobile the wordmark centres and the description disappears.

sections.description: The central object rotates through unrelated things (pepper mill, sling chair, sticker-covered hydrant, layered iced drink, record player, baseball cap), each photographed in the same light and replaced in place within a zone roughly 250-300px square. Shadow direction and visual weight stay constant, so the object is the page's only variable and no carousel controls are needed.

Beneath the object, a centred line of 11px grey text, a 30px gap, then a white field about 236 by 52px with 12px radius: light grey placeholder at left and a 26px circle-outlined arrow as the submit control inside the right end. No button label, border or shadow; the field is the only pure white on the page, which marks it as the one interactive thing.

steal: Build a pre-launch page from four elements only (wordmark top-left, one-line description top-right, a single centred object, an email field) and leave the rest of the screen empty.
Cycle one consistently lit cut-out object in the same spot to show range without adding a grid or carousel controls.
Make the email field the only pure-white element on an off-white page, with submit as a circled arrow inside it rather than a labelled button.

references.name: Le Petit Bleu
references.idea: The cafe's teal-and-white stripes become the whole system: one teal ink on cream, everything boxed in thin double outlines like printed menu cards, beside a permanently visible photo of the room.
references.hero: Viewport split 50/50 with 12px gaps. Left: a cream panel with a thin pale-teal outline and rounded corners. Inside, a second outlined box is the nav bar: two-line hamburger left, teal brush-script logo about 300px wide centred, a caps order link right. Below, a two-line light serif headline at about 3.5vw, centred, in teal, then two centred stacks, each a bold caps label, a serif line and a solid teal button wrapped in a second thin outline. Right: a full-height rounded photo of a striped booth, with an outlined hours bar across its top, three slide dots bottom-left and a white address card bottom-right.
references.type: Self Modern, a light bookish serif, for headline and 15px body; Matter SQ bold caps for labels and buttons; Archive Mono Pro typewriter caps for menu rows; a brush-script logo. Section titles are tall condensed serif caps sized so four to seven letters fill the column.
references.colour: #fcfbf7 #13a7b2 #058599 #cfe5e7 #e9b81f — Cream paper and a single teal used for every word, rule, outline and button; no black anywhere. Yellow, floral reds and marble enter only through the interior photographs.
references.imagery: Bright, saturated interior and food photographs; the right-hand panel is a full-height slideshow with rounded corners. Small food shots sit in a horizontal strip, and a fine line drawing of the shopfront with one teal awning fills a card.
references.layout: The left half scrolls as a stack of outlined cream cards (full-width or two-up) with 12px gaps while the right half stays fixed. Card contents are centred. A sticky nav card rides over the stack. On mobile the photo becomes the hero card's background.

sections.description: A card containing only the section word in tall condensed serif caps, teal, sized so its four letters fill the column edge to edge. Below it, a stack of full-width outlined rows about 36px high, each with a category name in typewriter mono caps at left and a thin plus sign at right, separated by 6px gaps. Above the title: a ticker row of tiny caps and a strip of four small food photos with rounded corners.

The same giant condensed title treatment, then centred serif paragraphs in teal with underlined links in a narrow measure of about 280px. Further down, a landscape photo of the two proprietors with a centred two-line caption in tiny sans, followed by more centred paragraphs. All of it lives in the left half while the right photo panel has advanced to a shelf-wall image.

A header row with a tiny bold caps label at left and a script follow-us link with arrow at right, then three portrait images (about 3:5) with 12px rounded corners in a row, the third cropped by the column edge to imply a carousel. Directly below, the next giant section title begins and is cropped by the viewport.

steal: Print everything in one brand ink on cream, including body text, rules and buttons, and let photographs supply the other colours.
Wrap buttons and panels in a second thin outline offset by a few pixels to get a printed-ticket feel.
Keep a tall photo panel fixed on one half and scroll a stack of cards on the other, swapping the photo as sections change.

references.name: Transport
references.idea: Present a USB stick as a luxury object: one studio render on charcoal above a chrome custom wordmark, then let moody macro photography carry the rest.
references.hero: Flat charcoal field. Centred slightly above the midline, a cut-out render of the drive about 31% of viewport width with its steel arm swung up at 30 degrees. Under it a chrome, ultra-wide custom wordmark spans 72% of the width on one line yet is only 45px tall. Then a centred serif tagline at 2.6vw and a single row: mono spec, a dark pill showing price and sold-out state, mono spec. Logo top-left, a grey centred nav prompt, a small pill with a glowing dot top-right. Carousel chevrons sit at the far left and right edges at product height. The bottom fifth is empty.
references.type: Three voices: a chrome extended techno wordmark as image; Untitled Serif 400 at 38px with -0.026em tracking for taglines and body; ISO mono for specs and caps eyebrows. Section heads switch to a tight heavy Untitled Sans near 36px. Nothing exceeds 3.6vw.
references.colour: #1c1c1c #c8c5ba #6e6f6a #5b5d45 #f1f1ef #2d2d2d — Charcoal base with white text; colour comes only from photographs in grey-olive, concrete and amber. One section flips to dark text over a pale blurred photo.
references.imagery: One clean product render, then shallow-focus macro photographs of the translucent drive on cutting mats, concrete and fabric, graded olive-grey with grain. Full-bleed bands with feathered edges, plus a row of rounded cards of unequal widths.
references.layout: Centred hero, then full-bleed photo bands each carrying one short text group placed differently: top-left, centre-right over a card, bottom-left, centred. Band edges dissolve through heavy blur instead of hard cuts. About 160 words across eleven screens.

sections.description: Full-bleed pale out-of-focus photograph with the drive in sharp focus in the lower half. Dark text overlays the top: a heavy tight grotesk heading at about 36px, left-aligned 8% in from the edge, then three equal columns, each a tiny glyph plus mono caps label over two lines of serif copy. No cards or dividers; the photo's soft blur is the only background.

A full-width macro photo band fades out through a blurred lower edge. On charcoal beneath it, one row of four rounded-corner image cards of unequal widths (one double-width, three single) with narrow gaps, each a tightly cropped lifestyle shot in a different colour temperature. The row is cut by the viewport bottom; further down one card grows taller and pins beside a short text group.

Dark band over a concrete-wall photograph. The drive render floats at top centre, half out of frame, with a horizontal motion streak smeared across the wall behind it. Text sits bottom-left: mono caps eyebrow, heavy grotesk heading, two lines of serif. The band cross-dissolves into an olive bokeh photo holding a centred mono equation, heading and one serif line whose quantities are joined by italic conjunctions.

Two small white script-lettered badges side by side at top centre, like garment labels, with a tiny pill link beneath, then a mostly empty charcoal field. Bottom-left, three tiny stacked mono link groups; bottom-right, white card-suit icons above a two-line italic mono credit, right-aligned.

steal: Pair one centred product cut-out with a very wide, very short metallic wordmark so the logo reads as an engraved nameplate.
Give three typefaces strict jobs: serif for sentences, mono for specs and eyebrows, heavy grotesk for section heads.
Blur the top and bottom edges of full-bleed photo bands so sections melt into each other with no hard seams.
